rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with an expanded blastocyst and visible zona thinning, but it overstates confidence in ICM/TE quality from a single image and adds speculative details (symmetry, pump activity, herniation points, absence of multinucleation/vacuolization) that are not clearly discernible.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, smoking, male factor context, endometrium, first-cycle status, and embryo grade into prognosis and management.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear pathway from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis; minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments and overinterpretation of some findings.

Mostly aligned with standard IVF practice: SET for a young patient with a good-quality day-5 blastocyst, no routine PGT-A at age 24, and emphasis on smoking cessation. Some recommendations are more individualized/speculative than guideline-based (e.g., routine progesterone level checks, IM progesterone due to BMI 29.2, making smoking cessation a prerequisite).
Provides clear and practical next steps for transfer, luteal support considerations, follow-up testing, lifestyle modification, and future stimulation-cycle optimization.
